page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.88 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the Xen hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, fall into the poor to weak categories. However, multi-core performance is more resilient, with the Passmark CPU score and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance reaching average tiers. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average performance, with cached read-only small block speeds of 388.0 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds of 50.08 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations and database simulations, such as Passmark database operations, also maintain average ratings.

Given its older hardware generation, the c3.2xlarge offers a legacy compute-optimized profile where local NVMe SSD storage is bundled directly. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation and fast local storage without needing the highest single-thread performance of modern architectures. It is suitable for multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and basic database operations, but is poorly suited for modern LLM inference or single-threaded, high-throughput applications.
description: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor and an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor. It delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 15.0 GB of memory, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.8 GHz, its performance profile is characterized by average multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core metrics. While single-threaded benchmarks like Geekbench single-core and bzip3 decompression score in the lower percentiles, multi-core operations, software compilation, and static web serving achieve average tier results. With a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance represents a legacy compute option with integrated local storage. It is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations where high single-core performance is not a primary requirement.
